body.en: Roots and fractional exponents are two notations for the same idea. Converting between them turns awkward radical problems into routine exponent arithmetic.
\( a^{m/n}=\sqrt[n]{a^{m}}=\big(\sqrt[n]{a}\big)^{m} \). The denominator is the root; the numerator is the power.

label.en: ▲ Algebra 2 Traps & Commandments — Radicals & Rational Exponents

body.en:
• Extraneous Roots from Squaring: Squaring both sides of an equation introduces spurious solutions (e.g. \(A = B \implies A^2 = B^2\), but \((-3)^2 = 3^2\) does not mean \(-3 = 3\)). You must plug every candidate back into the original un-squared radical equation!
  • Principal Non-Negative Root: \(\sqrt{x}\) always denotes the non-negative square root. If an equation simplifies to \(\sqrt{x} = -k\) (where \(k > 0\)), there are immediately no real solutions.
  • Absolute Value on Even Roots: \(\sqrt{x^2} = |x|\), not simply \(x\). In general, \(\sqrt[n]{x^n} = |x|\) whenever \(n\) is an even integer.
  • Isolate the Radical First: Never square an equation while a radical is added to other terms (e.g. \(\sqrt{x+1} + 3 = x\)). Always isolate the radical as \(\sqrt{x+1} = x - 3\) before squaring.

label.en: Worked Example C — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 4)(x - 9) = 0 \implies x = 4 \text{ or } x = 9 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 4 + 9 = \mathbf{13} \) and product \( = (4)(9) = \mathbf{36} \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 5)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \text{ or } x = 5 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 5 + 5 = \mathbf{10} \) and product \( = (5)(5) = \mathbf{25} \).

solution.en: Square both sides: \(3x+1=(x-1)^2=x^2-2x+1\Rightarrow x^2-5x=0\Rightarrow x=0\) or \(x=5\). Check \(x=0\): \(1=-1\) ✗ (extraneous). Check \(x=5\): \(4=4\) ✓. Solution: \(x=5\).

question.en: Solve the radical equation \(\sqrt{2x + 7} - x = 2\) for all real solutions and confirm extraneous roots.

solution.en:
Isolate the radical term:

\[\sqrt{2x + 7} = x + 2.\]

Square both sides:

\[2x + 7 = (x + 2)^2 = x^2 + 4x + 4.\]\[x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0 \implies (x + 3)(x - 1) = 0 \implies x = -3 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 1.\]

Test in the original un-squared equation:

  • Check \(x = -3\): \[\sqrt{2(-3) + 7} - (-3) = \sqrt{1} + 3 = 1 + 3 = 4 \neq 2. \quad \text{(Extraneous ✗)}\]
  • Check \(x = 1\): \[\sqrt{2(1) + 7} - 1 = \sqrt{9} - 1 = 3 - 1 = 2. \quad \text{(Valid ✓)}\]

The only valid real solution is \(x = 1\).

question.en: [Radicals & Rational Exponents · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Radicals & Rational Exponents · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
